citation: Li, Chan, Zhu, Pei, Ma, Liu, Shah (2023). Are ChatGPT and GPT-4 General-Purpose Solvers for Financial Text Analytics? A Study on Several Typical Tasks. EMNLP 2023 Industry Track. Read: arXiv 2305.05862v2 abstract page and ar5iv HTML
text_source: Public financial NLP sets: Financial PhraseBank, FiQA-SA, TweetFinSent, Headlines, FIN NER, REFinD, FinQA, ConvFinQA
feature: Sentiment, headline classification, NER, relation extraction, numeric QA
method: ChatGPT and GPT-4 zero-shot and few-shot (chain-of-thought on FinQA) against fine-tuned task models (FinBERT, RoBERTa, BERT, CRF, Luke, FinQANet) and BloombergGPT
outcome: Fine-tuned small models win on headlines (95.36 vs 86.00 F1), NER (82.70 vs 56.71) and relation extraction (56.30 vs 46.87); GPT-4 wins on FinQA (78.03 vs 68.90) and ConvFinQA (76.48 vs 61.24); sentiment about tied. Numbers as read from the HTML tables
informs_decision: Goal C; gap hypothesis (prompting only: no retrieval, no LLM fine-tuning, no tools, no open-weight LLM)

citation: Ovadia, Brief, Mishaeli, Elisha (2023). Fine-Tuning or Retrieval? Comparing Knowledge Injection in LLMs. arXiv 2312.05934v3 (January 2024). Read: abstract page and HTML
text_source: Wikipedia-derived: five MMLU subjects; 910 GPT-4-generated, manually verified current-events questions (August to November 2023)
method: Llama2-7B, Mistral-7B, Orca2-7B; base against unsupervised fine-tuning (continued pre-training on raw text), each with and without RAG (bge-large-en, FAISS); 0-shot and 5-shot on MMLU
outcome: RAG beats unsupervised fine-tuning; fine-tuned plus RAG scored below base plus RAG on current events for all three models (Mistral 0.875 vs 0.830); authors call top-k unstable; no intervals
pit_handling: Current-events questions postdate the models' training data; authors note some are answerable from prior knowledge
informs_decision: Method comparison: precedent for crossing fine-tuning with retrieval on open 7B models; fine-tuning without retrieved context can interact negatively with retrieval

citation: Balaguer et al. (2024). RAG vs Fine-tuning: Pipelines, Tradeoffs, and a Case Study on Agriculture. arXiv 2401.08406v3. Read: abstract page and HTML full text
text_source: Agricultural documents (USA, Brazil, India); 273 human-curated Washington-state questions for evaluation
method: Llama-2-chat 13B, Vicuna, GPT-4 untuned; Llama2 13B and GPT-4 fine-tuned; each with and without RAG (top 3, FAISS); GPT-4 judges full correctness
outcome: GPT-4 accuracy 75 (base), 80 (RAG), 81 (fine-tuned), 86 (both); fully correct 36, 60, 45, 61; retrieval recall at 3 of 81.5%; intervals of 2 to 5 points with unexplained construction
informs_decision: Method comparison (two-by-two precedent; separate retrieval measurement); interactions not modelled; commercial fine-tuning exists; teacher and judge circularity

citation: Zhang, Patil, Jain, Shen, Zaharia, Stoica, Gonzalez (2024). RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG. arXiv 2403.10131v2. Read: abstract page and HTML
text_source: PubMed QA, HotpotQA, Gorilla API benchmarks (HuggingFace, Torch Hub, TensorFlow Hub)
method: Llama2-7B fine-tuned on questions with the golden document plus distractors (golden document kept in a fraction P of examples), chain-of-thought targets written by GPT-4; against untuned, untuned plus RAG, domain fine-tuning without context (DSF), DSF plus RAG, GPT-3.5 plus RAG
outcome: RAFT best of the Llama variants on all five sets; DSF plus RAG scored below DSF alone on four of five (for example HuggingFace 61.06 to 42.59); training with distractors made the model more robust to the number of test-time documents; no intervals
informs_decision: Method comparison: the fine-tuned level needs a defined training prompt (with supplied and distractor passages) or the fine-tuning by retrieval cells are confounded

citation: Wang, Patel, Zha, Yang, Liu (2025). FinLoRA: Benchmarking LoRA Methods for Fine-Tuning LLMs on Financial Datasets. arXiv 2505.19819v1. Read: abstract page and HTML main text (appendices not available in HTML)
text_source: 19 financial sets: sentiment, headlines, NER, CFA and CPA exams, FiNER and FNXL tagging, FinanceBench, and four new XBRL sets from 2019-2023 10-K filings of Dow Jones 30 companies
feature: Classification, NER, XBRL tag and value extraction, formula construction and calculation, exam QA
method: Llama 3.1 8B with LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA, rsLoRA (rank 8 or 4) against untuned Llama 3.1 8B and 70B, DeepSeek V3, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite, and vendor-fine-tuned Gemini; base-model prompting not described; no retrieval or tools
outcome: LoRA 8B above GPT-4o on 15 of 19 sets by point estimate (my count); XBRL value extraction 97 to 99% for GPT-4o, DeepSeek V3, Gemini and all tuned variants; LoRA below GPT-4o on NWGI, FNXL, formula construction, FinanceBench; no intervals or seeds; some test sets under 100 items; LoRA training about 15 hours and 15 dollars on four A5000 GPUs
pit_handling: Not addressed; split construction for the XBRL sets not described in the text read
informs_decision: Goal C (finance evidence, no margin or interval; ceiling on value extraction); gap hypothesis (fine-tuning only)

citation: Chen, Ma, Wang, Cohen (2023). Program of Thoughts Prompting: Disentangling Computation from Reasoning for Numerical Reasoning Tasks. TMLR 2023. Read: arXiv 2211.12588v4 abstract page and ar5iv HTML
text_source: Five math word-problem sets; FinQA, ConvFinQA, TATQA
feature: Numeric QA over text and tables
method: Few-shot and zero-shot prompting of Codex: chain-of-thought against program-of-thought with an external Python interpreter; self-consistency; ablation with open code models on math sets
outcome: FinQA 40.4 (chain-of-thought) to 64.5 (program-of-thought), ConvFinQA 45.6 to 64.6, TATQA 61.4 to 69.0; about 12% average gain across sets; 47% of remaining TATQA errors are value grounding; open code models far behind on GSM8K and SVAMP
incremental_to: Chain-of-thought prompting on the same model
informs_decision: Method comparison: tool factor has a large effect on numeric items; errors that remain are reading errors, which tools do not fix

citation: Mosbach, Pimentel, Ravfogel, Klakow, Elazar (2023). Few-shot Fine-tuning vs. In-context Learning: A Fair Comparison and Evaluation. Findings of ACL 2023. Read: arXiv 2305.16938v2 abstract page and HTML full text
text_source: MNLI, RTE, QQP; challenge sets HANS and PAWS-QQP
feature: Sentence-pair classification, in domain and out of domain
method: OPT 125M to 30B; pattern-based fine-tuning against in-context learning with the same models and the same 2 to 128 examples; 10 seeds; three checkpoint-selection rules; Welch t-tests
outcome: Under equal conditions the two methods generalise similarly; in-context learning wins mainly when a large model is set against a much smaller fine-tuned one; the selection rule changes how small fine-tuned models rank
incremental_to: Each method against the other on the same model
informs_decision: Method comparison: same development set and same number of development evaluations; fine-tuning factor on the same base model

citation: Phogat, Puranam, Dasaratha, Harsha, Ramakrishna (2024). Fine-tuning Smaller Language Models for Question Answering over Financial Documents. Findings of EMNLP 2024. Read: ACL Anthology page, arXiv 2408.12337v1 abstract page and HTML full text
text_source: FinQA, ConvFinQA, TATQA (company reports; gold passage and table supplied)
feature: Multi-step numeric QA by generated Python programs
method: Mistral 7B, Orca-2 7B and 13B, phi-3-mini, phi-3-medium: zero-shot, 4-shot, and LoRA fine-tuned on GPT-4-written programs filtered against gold answers; GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 baselines imported from the authors' earlier paper
outcome: FinQA: fine-tuned students 71.57 to 77.59 against GPT-4 77.51 zero-shot and 78.46 few-shot; few-shot lowered accuracy for three of five students; no intervals or seeds
incremental_to: Zero-shot and few-shot versions of the same models; GPT-4 teacher
pit_handling: Not addressed; benchmarks predate all models
informs_decision: Goal C (point estimate only); equal development budget; teacher-label circularity; tool factor never switched off

citation: Sturm, Pichlmeier, Bernhard, Karalashvili, Klepsch, Groh, Luckow (2026). Assessment of RAG and Fine-Tuning for Industrial Question-Answering-Applications. AAAI 2026 Workshop on New Frontiers in Information Retrieval. Read: arXiv 2605.09533v1 abstract page and HTML
text_source: Two closed automotive sets: car manuals (1,417 test items) and vehicle-quality tickets (2,294 test items); question-answer pairs generated by GPT-4o
method: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA-3.3-70B, LLaMA-3.2-3B, each as base, fine-tuned, RAG, and fine-tuned plus RAG (16 systems per set); GPT models tuned through the Azure API with default settings, LLaMA with LoRA rank 64; GPT-4o as judge; z-tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction; extended cost-of-pass metric
outcome: Commercial models lead untuned; with RAG the open models reach what the authors call parity, resting on a non-significant difference (p = 1.000 for GPT-4o RAG against LLaMA-70B RAG on manuals); RAG judged the most effective and cheapest adaptation; accuracy values are in figures only and were not read
pit_handling: Authors note manual content may be in pre-training data; no cutoff analysis
informs_decision: Method comparison (closest design precedent: model by fine-tuning by retrieval, open and commercial); Goal C (parity claimed without a margin); retrieval top-k differed between the GPT and LLaMA stacks

citation: Islam, Kannappan, Kiela, Qian, Scherrer, Vidgen (2023). FinanceBench: A New Benchmark for Financial Question Answering. arXiv 2311.11944v1. Read: abstract page and ar5iv HTML. Belongs mainly to stream 04; deep note left to that stream
text_source: 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K filings and earnings reports of public companies, 2015 to 2023; 10,231 questions, 150 evaluated by hand
method: GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4, Claude2, Llama2 70B under closed book, single and shared vector store, long context, and oracle (evidence pages supplied); human grading; no fine-tuning
outcome: GPT-4-Turbo correct: 9% closed book, 19% shared vector store, 50% single vector store, 79% long context, 85% oracle; Llama2 19% and 41% on the two vector stores
incremental_to: Closed-book answer from the same model
pit_handling: Authors say it is unclear how much of the data is in pre-training; closed-book accuracy reported, not analysed
informs_decision: Method comparison: precedent for retrieval at three levels (none, retrieved, correct passage supplied) and for separating retrieval from reading

citation: Pecher, Srba, Bielikova (2025). Comparing Specialised Small and General Large Language Models on Text Classification: 100 Labelled Samples to Achieve Break-Even Performance. EMNLP 2025. Read: arXiv 2402.12819v4 abstract page and HTML (first 100,000 characters)
text_source: Eight English classification sets: SST2, MRPC, CoLA, BoolQ, AG News, TREC, SNIPS, DBPedia
method: Fine-tuning (BERT, RoBERTa), instruction-tuning (Flan-T5, Mistral-7B, Zephyr-7B with LoRA), prompting and in-context learning (including GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA-2 13B, LLaMA-3 8B); 10 to 100 repeated runs; break-even on means and on mean plus or minus one standard deviation
outcome: Specialised small models reach the general models at about 100 labels on average; counting variance raises the requirement by 100 to 200%; larger models not consistently better or less variable; 4-bit quantisation has negligible impact
incremental_to: General models used by prompting or in-context learning
pit_handling: Authors list possible pre-training contamination as a limitation
informs_decision: Goal C (a match claim should account for variance; quantisation re-run likely low risk); training-set size

citation: Huang, Drietomsky, Barrett, Wang (2026). How Small Can You Go? LoRA Fine-Tuning 270M-8B Models for Merchant Information Extraction in Financial Transactions. ICDM 2026. Read: arXiv 2606.08051v4 abstract page and HTML
text_source: Bank transaction descriptors with ten human-labelled fields; 6,125 train, 668 validation, 1,222 test
method: LoRA (rank 8, 6 epochs, LLaMA-Factory on one DGX Spark) on Gemma 3 270M to 4B, Qwen 3.5 0.8B to 4B, Aya, LLaMA 3.1-8B; two prompt templates; zero-shot versions of each; no few-shot and no commercial model
outcome: Qwen 3.5 4B 96.60% F1 against 96.75% for the rank-8 8B model; best zero-shot 0.758 F1; prompt template moves fine-tuned F1 by 0.2 to 1.8 points; reported score is the best of 12 checkpoints chosen on the test subset; no intervals or seeds
incremental_to: Zero-shot versions of the same models; a larger fine-tuned model
informs_decision: Method comparison (LoRA on Qwen 3.5 works on another stack; prompt by fine-tuning interaction is small after tuning; selection on test is the practice to avoid)
